title: Africa’s mineral strength is wasted if countries don’t work together – new report
summary: Transition minerals are found in 48 African countries, but most still export them raw and capture little value. Drawing on a World Bank–commissioned study, the authors argue that only regional cooperation, shared infrastructure and coordinated policy can turn mineral wealth into regional value chains.
keyPoints: Most individual countries hold small global shares of each mineral, which weakens their bargaining power alone.
Local refining adds value: Congolese cobalt roughly triples in price after refining.
Pooled trade policy, shared processing centres and partnerships with local processing and skills transfer are proposed.
